subject: Urdu Language & Literature – for centres in Pakistan

outcomes.text: Understand factual information and abstract ideas in texts about general topics.
Locate and select relevant information and details from one or more longer texts.
Recognise emotions, opinions and attitudes that texts state or strongly imply.
Understand arguments and conclusions in discursive texts and distinguish facts from opinions.
Understand formal and informal texts across a variety of forms.
Infer meanings of unfamiliar words from context across different topics.
Understand a broad range of vocabulary on general subjects.
Understand varied language structures, including some complex sentence forms.
Understand detailed information and abstract ideas in lengthy, complex texts on general and specific subjects.
Select relevant information and details from longer texts in varied formats.
Identify subtle details, including attitudes and explicit or implied opinions.
Interpret arguments and conclusions in discursive texts and distinguish facts from opinions.
Understand lengthy texts written in different styles for varied purposes.
Infer unfamiliar words and expressions from context across a wide range of topics.
Understand extensive vocabulary on general and more specific subjects.
Understand a wide range of complex language structures.
Communicate factual information, ideas, opinions and arguments about general subjects.
Develop arguments with relevant supporting details and examples.
Write detailed descriptions and narratives about real or imaginary events and experiences.
Organise ideas into coherent paragraphs and longer texts using cohesive devices.
Use register and style appropriate to the purpose and genre.
Use broad general-topic vocabulary with good accuracy.
Use varied grammatical structures, including some complex forms, accurately.
Produce writing with good control of spelling and punctuation.
Communicate information, ideas, opinions and arguments about complex subjects.
Develop and evaluate arguments, supporting viewpoints with reasons and relevant examples.
Write assured, personal and natural descriptions and narratives of real or imaginary experiences.
Create fluent arguments, descriptions and narratives with clearly linked paragraphs and cohesive devices.
Apply register, style and genre conventions appropriately for the text’s purpose.
Use extensive vocabulary, including idioms, accurately across general and specific topics.
Use a wide range of complex grammatical structures accurately.
Produce texts with highly accurate spelling and punctuation.
Understand how adverbs are formed and use them accurately.
Form and use interrogative adverbs accurately.
Use quantifiers and intensifiers appropriately in Urdu sentences.
Form and use comparative and superlative expressions accurately.
Recognise and use compound adverbs formed through repetition.
Use subject pronouns accurately in Urdu.
Use pronouns correctly as direct and indirect objects.
Recognise and use reflexive pronouns accurately.
Recognise and use possessive pronouns accurately.
Recognise and use interrogative pronouns accurately.
Recognise and use relative pronouns accurately.
Recognise and use demonstrative pronouns accurately.
Recognise and use indefinite pronouns accurately.
Recognise and use regular and irregular verbs accurately.
Apply correct agreement between verbs and their subjects.
Use modal verbs expressing obligation, including equivalents of “should” and “must”.
Use present and other tenses accurately in Urdu.
Use relative, subject, object, demonstrative, reflexive, indefinite, possessive and interrogative pronouns accurately.
Use regular and irregular verbs accurately.
Ensure verbs agree correctly with their subjects.
Use modal verbs, including should and must, appropriately.
Use present, present perfect, past, past perfect, future and future perfect tenses accurately.
Form and use present, past and future conditional structures.
Use continuous tenses, including perfect continuous forms, in present, past and future contexts.
Use verbal paraphrases and understand their functions.
Use verbal phrases as adverbs or adjectives.
Use a variety of introductory expressions.
Use coordinating conjunctions accurately.
Use subordinating conjunctions accurately.
Use compound conjunctions accurately.
Use correlative conjunctions accurately.
Use prepositions of place accurately.
Use prepositions of time accurately.
Use prepositions indicating movement accurately.
Use other prepositions accurately.
Use cardinal numbers accurately.
Use ordinal numbers accurately.
Apply agreement rules involving numbers.
Use expressions of quantity accurately.
Express dates accurately.
Express years accurately.
Use time expressions accurately.
Use comparative constructions accurately.
Use direct speech accurately.
Use indirect speech accurately.
Read varied literary texts independently with little support.
Discuss themes, characters, ideas and details while recognising genre conventions.
Develop arguments using relevant supporting details and textual examples.
Give a personal response and explain what is appreciated about a text.
Organise literary ideas into coherent paragraphs and longer responses.
Explain language choices and describe features that prompt reader responses.
Read literary texts fluently while appreciating implicit meanings and ideas.
Critically evaluate themes, characters, ideas and details with awareness of genre conventions.
Develop and support arguments by evaluating important themes and using detailed textual examples.
Offer a clear personal interpretation of themes and characters and explain reactions to the text.
Organise literary responses clearly using coherent paragraphs and suitable terminology.
Analyse language choices and evaluate how they engage the reader.
Discuss popular entertainment such as cinema, television, streaming, gaming and the internet.
Examine the role entertainment plays in people’s lives.
Consider celebrity culture, including role models, idols and public responsibilities.
Explore how people express identity through appearance, language, group membership and fashion.
Discuss preserving and respecting cultural heritage, monuments, festivals and traditions.
Explore theatre, music, visual arts, dance, literature and film.
Discuss access to the arts, funding, awards, representation and diversity.
Compare different diets and eating habits.
Examine food production’s environmental effects, organic food, waste and shortages.
Consider ethical food production, fair trade, labelling and government intervention.
Discuss friendships, family, relationships, generational differences and changing family patterns.
Examine quality of life, living environments, urban-rural differences, overcrowding and social isolation.
Explore lifestyle choices involving relationships, diet, fashion, self-expression, values and goals.
Discuss social organisation, law and order, governance and communities.
Explore national and global citizenship.
Examine the rights and responsibilities of individuals and governments.
Understand global warming, climate change, pollution, possible solutions, government action and economic effects.
Understand biodiversity and ecosystem conservation, including how animals are treated.
Understand how population growth affects the environment.
Understand natural-resource use, recycling, waste management, consumerism and excessive consumption.
Understand energy sources, their uses, geopolitics and effects on local environments and landscapes.
Understand ways to reduce environmental impact through individual choices about housing, food and travel.
Understand sustainable tourism, travel’s benefits and ways of protecting the world.
Understand tensions between international cooperation and national priorities on environmental issues.
Understand the respective environmental roles of individuals, industry, governments and environmental movements.
Understand medical advances and ethical issues surrounding scientific research.
Understand smart technology alongside related privacy and security concerns.
Understand artificial intelligence and its implications.
Understand the benefits and dangers of digital media.
Understand communication technologies and their uses.
Understand the nature and role of online communities.
Understand access to technology and related inequalities.
Understand how technology is used in education.
Understand how technology is used in the workplace.
